note: Adapted from the original description of Hodotermes viator by Sjöstedt (1900), which comprises a Latin diagnosis and a German description; nesting, gallery length, non-biting behaviour and other biological notes are not translated; measurements such as the mandible length of the soldier are omitted owing to OCR damage, and specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head brownish red, slightly darker anteriorly, almost flat, polished and shining, very flatly convex or square, sides almost straight, angles rounded, posterior margin rather weakly curved; the slightly flattened frons bears a rounded longitudinal ridge at the middle, with a depression on each side of the ridge; three fine lines arise from the middle of the head, one backward and two obliquely forward; labrum ligulate, slightly wider anteriorly, anterior margin only slightly rolled; ocelli represented only by two barely preserved dots; compound eyes flat, round, slightly compressed anteriorly; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head, entirely black, hardly paler even at the base, almost straight except for the fine incurved apex, left mandible with three teeth (one basal tooth very small), right mandible with two teeth besides the apex; pronotum 3/4 of the head width; transverse groove deep, anterior and posterior lobes about equal in length at the middle; anterior angles strongly deflexed and concave, rounded; posterior margin rounded; mesonotum and metanotum equal in size, as wide as the pronotum, oval, sides upturned, posterior margin slightly depressed at the sides and at the middle; body with thorax and legs pale reddish yellow; whole body almost completely smooth. Body length 10 mm, head with mandibles 5 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Almost indistinguishable from the worker of H. Aurivillii, size intermediate between the major and minor workers of that species; head not so fully dark brownish red as in major workers of H. Aurivillii; body reddish yellow, shining, smooth, only the legs slightly hairy; two specimens from the Cape have 27-segmented antennae; body length 8 mm, head width 4 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Upper surface nearly smooth, brown to yellowish brown, head and thorax slightly darker; mouthparts, antennae, anterior margin of the pronotum, apices of the tibiae, underside of the abdomen and tarsi yellowish; antennae 27-segmented; underside of the abdomen paler; wings hyaline, costa and marginal vein tinged with brown; radial vein giving off branches into the subcostal field before the middle of the wing; outer side of the tibiae spinose. Head almost circular, flatly convex, smooth, polished and shining; labrum rather densely and finely hairy; clypeus not swollen, truncate anteriorly; compound eyes slightly irregularly oval, flat, not much protruding; ocelli represented only by two small yellow spots, separated from the compound eye by a distance equal to the long diameter of the latter; antennae slightly longer than the head and pronotum together, 27-segmented, first segment large, cylindrical, second shorter, as long as wide, the following few segments very short rings, the remaining segments spherical, the terminal segment rather elongate; anterior lobe of the pronotum only slightly longer than the posterior lobe, width about twice the length; anterior lobe not reflexed, in lateral view in the same line as the posterior lobe; transverse groove deep, entering the anterior angles almost or completely; anterior margin more curved; anterior angles slightly deflexed, concave, slightly rounded, nearly right-angled; sides and posterior margin straight, posterior angles strongly rounded; in ventral view the upper surface almost smooth, the lower surface sparsely hairy; legs slightly more hairy; hind tibia with 5 apical and 3 lateral spines; wings hyaline with a greyish white tinge; at the wing scales of the fore wing 1 or 2 unbranched veins enter the costal field and soon join the marginal vein; subcosta giving off 3 oblique branches upward and about 5 downward, the last of which branches again; the first branches arise at or even before the middle of the wing; terminal branches anastomosing; media dividing into two branches at or before the middle of the wing, each branching again; submedia ending at the middle of the wing, giving off 7–10 mostly simple oblique branches, the outermost slightly curved. Wing span 34–40 mm, body with wings 19–22 mm, fore wing length 16–18 mm, width 3.8–4.5 mm, body with head 10–12 mm.
